Registering `prompt.submit` / `prompt.newline` with default keybinds (`enter`, `shift+enter`) makes them part of the global command keymap. Because these options don’t provide `onSelect` and aren’t marked `disabled`, pressing Enter while focus is *not* in an editable target will be intercepted by the global command handler (it calls `event.preventDefault()` when a keymap entry exists) and then effectively do nothing—breaking default Enter behavior across the app. Mark these command options as `disabled: true` (so they still appear in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts, but are excluded from the global keymap), or otherwise ensure they cannot be matched by the global command keymap.
```suggestion
      keybind: DEFAULT_PROMPT_SUBMIT_KEYBIND,
      disabled: true,
    },
    {
      id: PROMPT_NEWLINE_ID,
      title: language.t("command.prompt.newline"),
      keybind: DEFAULT_PROMPT_NEWLINE_KEYBIND,
      disabled: true,
```

Good catch — applied `disabled: true` on both registrations in b7e445b5. Excludes them from the global keymap build in `context/command.tsx` while `command.catalog` / `command.options` / `settings.current.keybinds` still surface them in the Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts UI (none of those iterate with a disabled filter). Local dispatch in `prompt-input.tsx` is unaffected — it reads keybinds from `settings.keybinds` directly, not from the registered command option.

`ConfigJsonError` now includes an optional `input` field, and `ConfigParse.jsonc()` populates it with the full raw config text. Since `ErrorMiddleware` serializes `NamedError` via `err.toObject()` and returns it to the client (and also logs the error object), this can leak secrets from config files (API keys, tokens) into HTTP responses and logs.

Consider removing `input` from the error payload entirely, or at least redacting/truncating it before `toObject()` is returned (e.g., keep only a short excerpt around the failing line/column, or keep `input` only in server-side logs with redaction).
```suggestion

```

The JSONC linter is currently configured to always allow JSONC features (`allowTrailingComma: true` and comments allowed by default). However, the backend enforces strict JSON when the global config file is `opencode.json`/`config.json` (it disallows comments/trailing commas based on the filename). This mismatch means the editor may show “no lint errors” for content that the server will reject on save.

Suggestion: configure the linter (and ideally the language mode) based on the loaded file extension (e.g., enable JSONC only when `path.endsWith('.jsonc')`, otherwise set `disallowComments: true` and `allowTrailingComma: false`).

Remove it, or use it consistently instead of duplicating the `Effect.runPromise(Config.Service.use(...))` call in `withGlobalTmp`.
```suggestion

```

`formatServerError(props.error, language.t)` won’t produce a useful message for `session.error` payloads coming from the SDK (e.g. `{name:"APIError"|"ProviderAuthError", data:{message}}`), since `formatServerError` currently only handles `Error`, `string`, and a couple of specific server error shapes. This will often log `"Unknown error"` even when the SDK provided a message. Consider deriving `message` from the SDK error shape (e.g. `error.data.message` when present) or extending the shared formatter to handle these SDK error objects, and avoid the `as {…; error?: unknown}` cast by using the narrowed `EventSessionError` type.
```suggestion
      const props = event.properties
      const sdkMessage =
        props.error &&
        typeof props.error === "object" &&
        "data" in props.error &&
        props.error.data &&
        typeof props.error.data === "object" &&
        "message" in props.error.data &&
        typeof props.error.data.message === "string"
          ? props.error.data.message
          : undefined

      console.error("[global-sync] session error", {
        scope: directory === "global" ? "global" : "workspace",
        directory: directory === "global" ? undefined : directory,
        project: directory === "global" ? undefined : getFilename(directory),
        sessionID: props.sessionID,
        message: sdkMessage ?? formatServerError(props.error, language.t),
```

`Effect.try`'s `catch` handler maps thrown exceptions to the *error channel*, not a fallback success value. Returning `raw.replace(...)` here means a JSON parse failure will cause the effect to fail with a string (and then `latestImpl` will `orDie`), rather than falling back to the cleaned version string as intended. Consider parsing in a normal `try/catch` and returning a successful fallback, or using `Effect.sync(...).pipe(Effect.catchAll(...))` to turn parse failures into a success value (and only fail when the result is truly invalid).

`Bom.syncFile()` runs *after* publishing `File.Event.Edited` / `FileWatcher.Event.Updated`. If the formatter drops the BOM, watchers/LSP may observe the BOM-less intermediate state. For consistency with `WriteTool` (which syncs before publishing events), run `Bom.syncFile` immediately after `format.file` and before publishing bus/watcher events, then use the synced content for the final diff metadata.

`waitForDocumentDiagnostics` only retries pulls when a new diagnostic registration arrives (`next !== "registration"` returns). If the server supports pull but the first pull times out/returns empty while the server is still computing, and it doesn’t change registrations or push diagnostics, this will exit early (on push timeout) without retrying within the overall 5s window. Consider polling/retrying pull requests (with a small backoff) until the overall timeout elapses.

`waitForFullDiagnostics` has the same early-exit behavior: after one pull sweep it returns unless registrations change. For pull-only servers that take longer than `DIAGNOSTICS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` (3s) to compute, this can cause `waitForDiagnostics` to return before the overall 10s timeout without ever seeing diagnostics. Consider retrying pull requests until the full timeout expires (or until a push arrives).
```suggestion
      const retryDelay = Math.min(DIAGNOSTICS_DEBOUNCE_MS, remaining)
      const next = await Promise.race([
        pushWait.then((ready) => (ready ? "push" : "timeout" as const)),
        waitForRegistrationChange(remaining).then((changed) => (changed ? "registration" : "timeout" as const)),
        new Promise<"retry">((resolve) => setTimeout(() => resolve("retry"), retryDelay)),
      ])
      if (next === "push" || next === "timeout") return
```

`requestWorkspaceDiagnosticReport` treats the request as `handled` only when `byFile.size > 0`. A successful `workspace/diagnostic` response with zero items (meaning “no workspace diagnostics”) would be considered unhandled, which can unnecessarily extend waits and can leave stale workspace pull diagnostics around. Consider setting `handled` based on receiving a valid report (e.g., `Array.isArray(report.items)`), not on whether any diagnostics were returned.

`Npm.which(pkg, bin)` checks `files.includes(bin)` for an exact match. On Windows, npm/bun typically creates shims like `pyright-langserver.cmd` (and/or `.ps1`) in `node_modules/.bin`, so this exact-match check can return `none` even though the requested bin exists. Consider matching against PATHEXT variants (or doing a prefix match + extension handling) so callers can pass the logical bin name and still resolve correctly cross-platform.

The TypeScript special-case stores the first `publishDiagnostics` into `pushDiagnostics` but returns without calling `updatePushDiagnostics`, so no `Event.Diagnostics` is published. `waitForFreshPush()` relies on that bus event to re-check `published`, which means `waitForDiagnostics()` can unnecessarily block until timeout even though diagnostics have already arrived. Consider still publishing the event (or remove this special-case and rely on debounce/version checks instead).
```suggestion
      updatePushDiagnostics(filePath, params.diagnostics)
```

In `formatFile`, `getFormatter()` already filters out disabled/false commands and returns only entries with a real `cmd`, so the `if (cmd === false) continue` branch is unreachable. Removing it (or changing `getFormatter`/types so `cmd` can actually be false here) will simplify control flow and avoid misleading readers about possible states.
```suggestion

```

`util/bom.ts` mixes pure string helpers (`split`/`join`) with Effect/AppFileSystem helpers (`readFile`/`syncFile`). This means modules that only need `split`/`join` (e.g. `src/patch/index.ts`) also pull in the Effect/filesystem dependencies. Consider splitting the Effect-based helpers into a separate module to keep the dependency surface smaller.

`createRefreshQueue()` now normalizes directories before enqueuing and then passes the normalized string into `input.bootstrapInstance(dir)`. That changes the directory value flowing into bootstrapping (and potentially SDK headers / persistence keys) rather than only normalizing internal queue keys. Consider storing the normalized key for de-duping while keeping the original directory string to pass to `bootstrapInstance` (or normalize only at Map/Set access sites in the caller).

When serving from `distDir`, `filePath` is built directly from `reqPath` via `path.join(distDir, ...)` without guarding against `..` segments. A request like `/../somefile` could traverse outside `app/dist` and read arbitrary files. Resolve and verify the resulting path stays within `distDir` (e.g., `resolved.startsWith(distDir + path.sep)`), and reject/404 otherwise.
`DEFAULT_CSP` is now unused (embedded UI uses `csp(..., false)` instead). Remove the unused constant to avoid confusion, or use it as the non-dev CSP source of truth to keep the policies consistent.

`mark()` stores lifecycle state under `dirKey(directory)` but calls `runEviction(directory)` with the un-normalized value. Since `children` keys are normalized and `runEviction()` compares `directory !== skip`, the intended “skip the directory we just touched” filter won’t work on Windows (and may immediately evict the just-marked store). Normalize `skip` before passing/comparing (e.g., call `runEviction(dirKey(directory))` or normalize inside `runEviction`).
```suggestion
    const key = dirKey(directory)
    lifecycle.set(key, { lastAccessAt: Date.now() })
    runEviction(key)
```
Fixed. The queue now uses a Map<normalized_key, original_directory> so deduplication uses the normalized key while bootstrapInstance still receives the original un-normalized directory string.
Fixed. Added path.resolve + startsWith check for both the main file path and the SPA fallback index.html path. Requests with .. segments that resolve outside distDir get a 403.
Fixed. Removed the unused DEFAULT_CSP constant. The embedded UI path now uses the same csp() function with extracted script hashes instead.

Fixed. mark() now passes the pre-normalized key to runEviction() instead of the raw directory string, and the runEviction filter comparison no longer double-normalizes. This was the actual bug on Windows: runEviction would skip the wrong directory because lifecycle keys were normalized but the skip comparison used the raw backslash path.

`node:fs/promises` does not provide `exists()`, so `fs.exists(appDistDir)` (and the other `fs.exists(...)` calls below) will throw at runtime when this route runs under the Node adapter. Use `fs.access()`/`fs.stat()` with try/catch (or a small helper) to implement an async existence check that works in both Bun and Node.

These backslashes will be included literally in the prompt string (e.g., it will print "\`bun typecheck\`") since backticks don’t need escaping inside double-quoted TS strings. Remove the backslashes so the prompt renders as intended.
```suggestion
    "After resolving the conflicts, run `bun typecheck` at the repo root.",
```

The prompt strings escape backticks with backslashes ("\`...") which will show up literally in the output. Backticks don’t need escaping in normal TS strings; drop the backslashes so the instructions render cleanly.
```suggestion
    "Run `bun typecheck` at the repo root.",
    "Run `./script/build.ts --single` in `packages/opencode`.",
```

PR description says the first emitted `tool_call` is now sent at `running`, but `toolStart()` still always emits a `tool_call` with `status: "pending"` (and tests assert a synthetic pending is emitted before the first running update). Either update the PR description to match the implemented behavior, or (if the intent really is to emit the initial tool_call as running) set the initial status based on `part.state.status` when first observed.

This test asserts `result.locations[0].path.startsWith("/")`, which assumes POSIX path formatting. Unit tests run on Windows in CI, where absolute paths typically look like `C:\...` or `\...`, so this will fail. Use `path.isAbsolute(...)` (and/or compare against `path.resolve(cwd, ...)`) instead of checking for a leading `/`.

These expectations hard-code POSIX absolute paths (e.g. `/workspace/project/src/index.ts`). On Windows, `path.resolve` will produce Windows-style absolute paths, so the test will fail even if the implementation is correct. Consider building the expected value with `path.resolve(cwd, ...)` (or normalizing via `path.normalize`) and asserting equality against that.

This assertion expects a POSIX absolute path (`/workspace/rel/file.ts`). If tests run on Windows, resolving `rel/file.ts` against a cwd will likely yield a Windows-style absolute path, causing failures. Build the expected path with `path.resolve(cwd, "rel/file.ts")` (and optionally normalize separators) so the test is platform-independent.

`abs()` checks `!p.startsWith("/")` to decide whether to resolve a path. This is not a reliable absolute-path check across platforms (Windows drive-letter/UNC paths, and paths starting with `\\`). The rest of the codebase typically uses `path.isAbsolute(...)` (and sometimes a drive-letter regex) for this. Consider switching to `isAbsolute(p)` for correctness and consistency.

For `bash`, `locations` is populated directly from `input.workdir` without resolving relative values against the passed `cwd`. Since other tools resolve relative paths (e.g. `filePath`) against `cwd`, this can produce inconsistent/incorrect locations when `workdir` is relative (including the common `"."`). Consider using the same `abs(..., cwd)` logic for `workdir` (and optionally treating `"."` as “no location”).
```suggestion
        locations: workdir ? [{ path: abs(workdir, cwd) }] : [],
```
Why do you skip loading env vars in nushell?

The PR description says the first `tool_call` is now emitted at `running`, but `toolStart()` still sends a `tool_call` event with `status: "pending"`. Either update the PR description to match the implementation, or change the emission logic so the first `tool_call` is actually sent with a running/in-progress status (and ensure clients still get a stable toolCallId/title/rawInput early).

The PR description mentions exposing the command plus its `cwd` in `rawInput`, but the `bash` formatter forwards `rawInput: input` unchanged and only includes a location when `workdir` is explicitly provided. If the command runs in the session cwd when `workdir` is absent (as the `bash` tool does), consider including that resolved cwd somewhere consistently (e.g., always add a location with `cwd`, and/or extend `rawInput` to include an explicit `cwd` field) so clients can see where the command is executing.

**Suggestion**: For consistency with lines 189-190 which use `as const`, consider adding `as const` to this object as well. This ensures TypeScript narrows the `type` property to the literal `"reasoning"` rather than `string`.

This is optional - it likely works fine without it due to contextual typing, but the inconsistency stands out.

`saveFilePickerDialog` is currently implemented via `open(...)`, which typically shows an “open” dialog rather than a “save” dialog and may not honor save semantics on all platforms. Consider using the dialog plugin’s save API (and passing through `title` as well) to match the method name/expected behavior.

`root!` assumes the `#root` element exists; if it doesn’t, this will throw at startup. It’d be safer to guard (e.g., throw a clear error or return early) when `document.getElementById("root")` is null instead of using a non-null assertion.

`tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` appears to be a generated TypeScript incremental build artifact, and it’s already listed in the repo root `.gitignore`. It shouldn’t be committed; please remove it from the PR and ensure the iOS package build output stays ignored.

`BUILD_OUTPUT` is hard-coded to a specific user’s DerivedData path, which will break for other developers/CI machines. Prefer deriving the app path from `xcodebuild` output (e.g., using `-derivedDataPath` to a local temp dir, or querying `BUILD_DIR`/`CONFIGURATION_BUILD_DIR`) instead of committing a machine-specific path.

The plugin `name()` returns a placeholder string ("Does not matter here"). Tauri uses plugin names for identification/debugging, so this should be a stable, meaningful identifier (and ideally unique) to avoid confusion or collisions.

`eprintln!("{backend_note:?}")` will print the string using debug formatting (including surrounding quotes / escapes). If this is meant to be a user-facing diagnostic, prefer display formatting (`{backend_note}`) so logs are cleaner.

The PR is labeled/docs-scoped, but it also adds a large new `packages/ios` app + generated Xcode/Tauri artifacts and binaries. This makes the change set much broader (and harder to review/revert) than “sync env vars with source code”. Please split the iOS app introduction into a separate PR (or update the PR title/description and rationale accordingly).

This re-export is self-referential (`./index` resolves to this same file), which will cause an import cycle / stack overflow or missing exports at runtime/build time. If you intended a barrel file, export from the actual entry module (e.g. `./index.tsx`) or remove this file.

Fix grammar in this comment: `dont` → `don't`.
```suggestion
  // When a user changes config from a value back to default in the Desktop app, we don't want to leave a blank `"shell": "",` key
```

`syncDisplayBackend` is resolving the `getDisplayBackend` function itself instead of calling it, so `displayBackend` can end up being set to a function rather than a `DisplayBackend` value. Call `platform.getDisplayBackend()` (or `platform.getDisplayBackend?.()`) and resolve that result before storing it.

The shell select's auto option label is hard-coded as `"Auto (Default)"` rather than using the i18n dictionary like the rest of this settings UI. Please add a translation key for this label and use `language.t(...)` so it localizes correctly.
```suggestion
  const autoOption = { id: "auto", value: "", label: language.t("settings.general.row.shell.autoDefault") }
```

`getRoslynLanguageServer()` can be invoked concurrently by both the `csharp` and `razor` servers. If the binary isn't installed yet, this can race and run multiple `dotnet tool install` processes in parallel. Consider adding a shared in-process cache/promise or a cross-process lock (e.g. Flock) around the install step so the tool is installed at most once.

The log message says "VS Code Razor extension not found", but the search targets `ms-dotnettools.csharp-*` (the VS Code C# extension) and its `.razorExtension` payload. Consider updating the message to reflect what is actually missing (e.g., "VS Code C# extension (with Razor bits) not found") to reduce confusion when troubleshooting.
```suggestion
      log.info("VS Code C# extension (with Razor support) not found, skipping Razor LSP")
```

Because `MessageV2.Assistant.fields.error` is an optional schema, wrapping it in `Schema.suspend(...)` will produce a `Suspend` node; with the current `Suspend -> z.lazy(...)` translation this can make the `error` key appear required in the derived Zod/OpenAPI schema. Please double-check the resulting JSON Schema `required` list for `session.error` (and adjust the `Suspend` walker so optionality is preserved).

`Suspend` is currently mapped to `z.lazy(() => walk(ast.thunk()))`, which hides the underlying `ZodOptional`/`ZodDefault` wrapper from parent `z.object(...)` construction. In practice this can turn suspended optional/default fields into *required* keys in derived Zod + JSON Schema (e.g. `Schema.optional(...)` inside `Schema.suspend`). Consider preserving top-level optional/default by inspecting `ast.thunk()` (e.g. if it’s optional/default, wrap the lazy with `.optional()` / `.default(...)` at the outermost layer) or by resolving the thunk during walking instead of at parse time.

`git log ... --format=%T`.text() is split on `\n` without trimming entries. If Git outputs CRLF (or trailing whitespace), `remoteTrees.indexOf(localTree)` can fail even when the tree exists, causing unnecessary smoke/push. Consider normalizing with `.split("\n").map(x => x.trim()).filter(Boolean)` before `indexOf`.

The “beta branch has identical contents” check only searches trees from `origin/dev..origin/beta`. When `origin/beta` is at (or behind) `origin/dev`, that range is empty, so an identical `origin/beta` tip tree won’t be detected and the script can still proceed to smoke/push. Consider also comparing `beta^{tree}` directly against `origin/beta^{tree}` (after fetch) as a fast path.

Same normalization issue as above: `remoteTreesAfterSmoke` is split without trimming/filtering, so `indexOf(validatedTree)` can fail on CRLF output and trigger an unnecessary force push. Trimming each line (and filtering blanks) would make this comparison robust.

`git push origin beta --force` can still clobber concurrent updates to `origin/beta` that land after your last fetch/check. Using `--force-with-lease` would provide a safety net against races while still allowing the intended overwrite when the remote tip hasn’t changed.

This table claims to be sorted alphabetically, but `OPENCODE_CLIENT` is out of order (it appears after `OPENCODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` and after the config-related vars). Please reorder the rows (or clarify the grouping/sorting rule) so readers can reliably scan the list.

`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` is parsed in code as a comma-separated list of `key=value` pairs (see `packages/opencode/src/effect/observability.ts`). The current description just says "headers", which doesn't convey the required format. Please update the description to document the expected syntax (and any escaping/encoding expectations).
```suggestion
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`          | string  | OpenTelemetry OTLP exporter headers as comma-separated `key=value` pairs; percent-encode reserved characters such as commas, equals signs, or spaces in values |
```

The env var table is still missing several non-experimental flags that exist in `packages/opencode/src/flag/flag.ts` (e.g. `OPENCODE_ALWAYS_NOTIFY_UPDATE`, `OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT`, `OPENCODE_SHOW_TTFD`, `OPENCODE_ENABLE_QUESTION_TOOL`). To keep docs in sync with the source, either add the missing variables here (with brief descriptions) or explicitly state that this table is not exhaustive and link to where the authoritative list lives.

`chainGuidance()` default branch still tells the model to use a “Bash call” (and references “Write before Bash”), but the tool name is now `shell`. This mismatch will push agents to emit the wrong tool name in examples; update the wording to consistently refer to the Shell tool (or interpolate via the template variables).

The bash-profile `createPrExample` heredoc snippet appears truncated (it opens `cat <<'EOF'` but never closes the heredoc / quotes). Since `shell.txt` inlines `${createPrExample}` verbatim, this will render an invalid example in the tool prompt and may degrade PR-creation behavior. Suggest including the full, syntactically complete command example (closing `EOF` + `)"`), or switch to a safer pattern (e.g. `--body-file`) like the cmd.exe profile does.

In `profile()`’s fallback branch, the `intro` text hard-codes “bash command”, but this branch runs for any non-PowerShell/non-cmd shell name (e.g. `zsh`, `sh`). This makes the rendered tool prompt inaccurate on common macOS/Linux defaults; consider switching to “shell command” wording or deriving it from `shellDisplayName(name)`.

`ShellKind.ids` doesn’t include `cmd`, but `Shell.name()` can return `cmd` (e.g. when falling back to `cmd.exe` on Windows). That means `ShellKind.from("cmd")` silently coerces to `bash`, which can lead to incorrect shell-specific behavior (arity rules, prompts, etc.). Consider adding `cmd` to `ShellKind.ids` (and any related sets like `ps`) so shell-kind detection matches the actual shell selection logic.
```suggestion
  export const ids = ["bash", "cmd", "pwsh", "powershell"] as const
```

`touchesGuardrailRuntime` only matches commands containing the literal substring `.opencode/guardrails/` (note the trailing slash). Mutating commands like `rm -rf .opencode/guardrails` or `rm -rf ./.opencode/guardrails` will not be detected, allowing guardrail runtime mutation to slip through. Consider using a more robust path matcher (e.g., regex for `\.opencode/guardrails(?:/|\b)` after normalization) and reusing it for all guardrail-runtime checks.

The early-return guard `if (!cfg.some(...) && !touchesGuardrailRuntime) return` relies on `touchesGuardrailRuntime` being correct. With the current substring check, a mutating command against `.opencode/guardrails` (without trailing slash) can bypass the later mutation block and return here, effectively allowing protected runtime mutation. Fixing the guardrail-runtime path detection should close this bypass.

This README link points to an absolute local filesystem path (`/Users/.../packages/guardrails/managed/opencode.json`), which will be broken for other developers and when published. Switch it to a repo-relative link (e.g. `managed/opencode.json`) or a GitHub URL.
```suggestion
Copy [managed/opencode.json](managed/opencode.json) into the system managed config directory:
```

| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOCOMPACT` | boolean | Onemogući automatsko sažimanje konteksta |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE` | boolean | Onemogući automatske provjere ažuriranja |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE` | boolean | Onemogući čitanje iz `.claude` (prompt + vještine) |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT` | boolean | Onemogući čitanje `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS` | boolean | Onemogući učitavanje `.claude/skills` |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS` | boolean | Onemogući podrazumijevane dodatke (plugins) |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS` | boolean | Onemogući učitavanje vještina iz npm paketa |
| `OPENCODE_DISABLE_LSP_DOWNLOAD` | boolean | Onemogući automatsko preuzimanje LSP servera |
